routes.label: Assign grid coordinates and use shoelace
Split the polygons into grid pieces

question:
Which of the following polygons has the largest area?

[Figure 1](figures/2002_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Use one grid spacing as the length unit, so a grid square has area \(1\). Splitting along grid lines lets us compare exact areas using rectangles and right triangles. A triangle with perpendicular sides of length \(1\) has area \(\tfrac12\).

For \(A\), the bottom band consists of a \(2\times1\) rectangle and two half-square triangles. The narrow stem above it is a \(1\times2\) rectangle. Thus
\[
\text{Area of }A=2+\tfrac12+\tfrac12+2=5.
\]
For \(B\), the bottom band is a \(4\times1\) rectangle. Above it are two half-square triangles, giving
\[
\text{Area of }B=4+\tfrac12+\tfrac12=5.
\]
For \(C\), split along the vertical grid line through the two inward corners. The left piece fills a \(1\times4\) rectangle except for two half-square corners, so its area is \(4-1=3\). The right piece fits inside a \(2\times3\) rectangle. Its two missing corners are right triangles, each with base and height \(2\), so each has area \(2\). Therefore
\[
\text{Area of }C=(4-1)+(6-2-2)=5.
\]
For \(D\), the middle horizontal band is a \(3\times1\) rectangle. There are two half-square triangles above it and one below it. Hence
\[
\text{Area of }D=3+3\left(\tfrac12\right)=\tfrac92.
\]
For \(E\), split along the vertical grid lines through the endpoints of its lower sloping edge. The central piece is a \(1\times4\) rectangle with a half-square triangle removed at the bottom. The upper-left piece is a half-square triangle. The right piece is a \(1\times2\) rectangle with a half-square triangle removed. Thus
\[
\text{Area of }E=(4-\tfrac12)+\tfrac12+(2-\tfrac12)=\tfrac{11}{2}.
\]
Each split covers its polygon without overlapping interiors. Since \(\tfrac{11}{2}>5>\tfrac92\), polygon \(E\) has the largest area, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
